study.question: Does explicitly restoring the single discarded coarse-moment orientation bit selectively recover click AUC after axis canonicalization, under equal learned capacity and the fixed one-view recipe?
study.hypothesis: Observed g1-r0067-coarse_axis lost0.0018213522 AUC against g1-r0067-signed_bridge, while local_axis lost0.0005698974 and joint_axis lost0.0028001029. Earlier selective sign averaging also lost quality. These conditional results do not distinguish missing signed information from chart/optimization changes. For coarse moment m, choose s in{-1,+1} from the lowest-index largest-absolute coordinate, and c=s*m. The pair(c,s) exactly determines m=s*c at any finite parameter state. If missing coarse orientation is accessible and useful, a scalar s supplied alongside c should help more than supplying the same redundant scalar alongside m. A constant+1 column controls width, scale and trainable offsets. The hypothesis remains untested; no novelty, chronology or full-order-invariance claim.

nearest_work.difference: Archived v4 lines250-282 inspected: target-local weighted pooling without softmax and its dataset-specific LSTM-null report. We retain the inherited adaptation, task-specific gradients and context/history interaction; add an information-restoration factorial, not a reproduction or transferred LSTM conclusion.

Authorized section2.3 only: stacked and layer-wise interaction families provide context. The present change is a scalar chart-sign side input within the existing joint model, not a new tokenizer/attention stack.

Pinned benchmark forward113-159 inspected: target attention, field/task tokenization and interaction blocks. No HiFormer module adopted. Original paper full text unavailable in this registry; priority beyond this checked overlap remains unverified.

Pinned benchmark forward175-200 inspected: flattened item history and user fields feed chunk tokenization. We preserve compressed/moment pathways and test one bit, rather than flattening or adding paired streams. Original method paper is link/provenance only.

Read complete supplied ancestor and receipt: same max-absolute-pivot canonical coarse representation. Proposed variants retain all five existing summaries and add one scalar to both actual learned moment consumers; factorial signed controls isolate added capacity and redundant-bit conditioning.

inherited_components: All g0-r0052-block_nonlinear_transfer learned modules and copied initialized weights, ten-block compression, target-local action-aware scorer, native Dice support-folding and inference pruning
All five summaries, their coefficients, support gates and scaling; local and quadratic moments remain signed and unchanged
Four task adapters/towers, rank16 context/history interaction, auxiliary scorer/item/action/tower-context gradient blocks and adapter-context transfer
g1-r0067-coarse_axis max-absolute detached pivot convention and fresh item mapping to avoid caller mutation
Default host sum of four BCEs; no custom loss, labels or extra data used by forward
study.proposed_difference: Four cells cross coarse canonicalization with scalar sign availability. After constructing raw summaries, compute c=s*m and supply c or m; append s or +1 to residual_features and history_features before either consumer, including every auxiliary route and block-broadcast shared details. Widen only each residual first Linear and history projection Linear by one input column initialized to zero, copying all original weights/biases after original construction within a new CPU RNG fork. No parameter is added elsewhere and no original summary is replaced. All cells add4*(16+16)=128 dense weights: expected32192549 total/399333 dense/31793216 embedding, subject to native host count. No event/action/mask permutation or new order input.
predictions: All cells initialize to their corresponding old signed/coarse-axis predictions and gradients on old weights when the added columns are zero. Native host parity must be checked at shared parameters before training, including learned nonzero adapter/output weights.

At any finite fixed state c*s reconstructs raw m (up to arithmetic signs including signed zero); axis_only with constant input cannot recover the deliberately omitted bit from that vector alone. Other retained paths may carry overlapping order information.

If a useful missing bit explains an appreciable part of the coarse-axis loss, axis_with_sign improves more than signed_with_sign improves over its constant control; predeclare G0>0.001, I>=0.0005 and G1<=0.5G0 as the practical rescue pattern.

Expected cost remains close to the single-view384-404s ancestors and well below the597-617s two-view controls, but only native measured train/wall/GPU seconds, peak memory and latency establish this. No equal-compute superiority is claimed.

Pre-existing empty/1-16/17-64/>64 bins will be descriptive only. Coarse-axis loss was concentrated in long histories; selective rescue there is a prediction, not a confirmed mechanism. Report every slice sample/positive/negative count and all four metrics.
falsifiers: No selective interaction or no gap closure falsifies the predicted practical rescue for this implementation/recipe; it does not refute information sufficiency or all useful event order.
Comparable gains in both sign-bit cells favor generic redundant conditioning or optimization rather than a specific missing-bit account.
If the active constant changes the baseline gap substantially, the old sign-removal result is not a matched baseline for this wider architecture.

Failure of raw recovery, shape/dtype/device/input immutability/masking/gradient gates, initialization parity or added-count checks invalidates causal interpretation; do not train a failing implementation.
If only throughput or latency worsens, report quality and cost separately; no efficiency benefit may be inferred from small parameter overhead.
alternative_explanations: Learned embeddings determine the pivot; canonical charts and the detached sign bit change at pivot/sign boundaries.
Information availability does not ensure the fixed width16 nonlinear consumers learn sign-conditioned reconstruction in one epoch.
The constant scalar adds a learnable offset to the history projection; signed_constant is an active-capacity control, not an exact training replay of the incumbent.
Other position-dependent summaries/compression remain, so this does not isolate all order information or establish whole-model order invariance.
One frozen seed and reused validation selection; differences are provisional until authorized repetitions and paired user-cluster uncertainty are available.

The one-bit conditioning can regularize different chart regions, and a positive interaction is controlled predictive evidence rather than a proof of the data-generating mechanism. The supplied order lacks timestamps and the offline action policy may not transfer to production.

canonicalize_coarse=True, expose_coarse_sign=True. Prospective unmeasured four-cell study; no training or withheld access in this coding phase. Scalar selection and coarse chart are constant across train/eval: no prediction-only perturbation. Verify old-weight/input gradients (away from sign/pivot boundaries), native Dice population/running buffers, and gradient gates. Appended scalar weights should have finite possibly nonzero gradients and must be excluded from old-subspace one-step parity after first update. At a fixed state set scalar columns to zero for functional parity; do not claim trained wider constants are identical to old models. Verify checkpoint round-trip and RNG preservation.
